plan.goal: Synthetic example: make language practice consistent during a fictional irregular week.

moves.title: Attach practice to an existing cue
moves.concrete_move: Reserve a ten-minute practice block immediately after one existing daily cue.
moves.why_overlooked: The plan is treated as a separate appointment instead of a cue-linked habit.
moves.test_48h: Try the cue-linked block twice within 48 hours.
moves.success_signal: Both blocks start within fifteen minutes of the cue.
moves.stop_condition: Stop if either block displaces a non-negotiable commitment.
moves.evidence_status: The cue and schedule are prompt-supported; the adherence expectation is an inference. All numeric experiment values are synthetic planning assumptions, not measured outcomes.
moves.bounds: Twenty minutes total, no purchase, and no changes to other people's schedules.

experiment.hypothesis: The proposed precommitment mechanism may improve practice blocks starting within fifteen minutes of the cue.
experiment.metric: practice blocks starting within fifteen minutes of the cue
experiment.rollback: Remove the temporary practice aid and return to the previous private routine.

moves.title: Remove the setup step
moves.concrete_move: Prepare one small practice card before the next irregular day begins.
moves.why_overlooked: People often optimize content variety before reducing startup friction.
moves.test_48h: Use the prepared card for two short sessions.
moves.success_signal: The session begins without a search or selection step.
moves.stop_condition: Stop if the card causes confusion that cannot be resolved from supplied material.
moves.evidence_status: The setup friction is an inference to test, not an established fact. All numeric experiment values are synthetic planning assumptions, not measured outcomes.
moves.bounds: One card and twenty minutes of preparation.

experiment.hypothesis: The proposed subtraction mechanism may improve sessions starting without a search step.
experiment.metric: sessions starting without a search step
experiment.rollback: Remove the temporary practice aid and return to the previous private routine.

moves.title: Use a visible completion mark
moves.concrete_move: Place one mark on a private weekly strip after each completed session.
moves.why_overlooked: Progress is usually reviewed only after a missed week.
moves.test_48h: Record the mark immediately after two sessions.
moves.success_signal: The mark is recorded within five minutes of completion.
moves.stop_condition: Stop if the strip creates pressure that reduces honest reporting.
moves.evidence_status: The proposed feedback loop is a hypothesis. All numeric experiment values are synthetic planning assumptions, not measured outcomes.
moves.bounds: Use paper or an existing note, with no public sharing.

experiment.hypothesis: The proposed feedback mechanism may improve completion marks recorded within five minutes.
experiment.metric: completion marks recorded within five minutes
experiment.rollback: Remove the temporary practice aid and return to the previous private routine.

moves.title: Set a minimum viable session
moves.concrete_move: Define a two-minute fallback session that preserves the same practice target.
moves.why_overlooked: Consistency plans often treat a short session as failure instead of a bounded fallback.
moves.test_48h: Use the fallback once when the planned block is unavailable.
moves.success_signal: The fallback completes without extending the day or changing the target.
moves.stop_condition: Stop if the fallback repeatedly replaces the intended session.
moves.evidence_status: The fallback may reduce all-or-nothing behavior; this is an inference. All numeric experiment values are synthetic planning assumptions, not measured outcomes.
moves.bounds: Two minutes and one fallback per week.

experiment.hypothesis: The proposed constraint removal mechanism may improve fallback sessions completed without extending the day.
experiment.metric: fallback sessions completed without extending the day
experiment.rollback: Remove the temporary practice aid and return to the previous private routine.

moves.title: Review the next obstacle first
moves.concrete_move: Before the next session, write one likely interruption and a single response.
moves.why_overlooked: Planning usually lists ideal conditions rather than the next failure mode.
moves.test_48h: Write one response and use it if the named interruption appears.
moves.success_signal: The response is usable without inventing a new plan during the interruption.
moves.stop_condition: Stop if the response creates additional commitments or affects another person without consent.
moves.evidence_status: The interruption is prompt-supported only if stated by the user; otherwise it is speculation. All numeric experiment values are synthetic planning assumptions, not measured outcomes.
moves.bounds: Five minutes of planning and no external commitments.

experiment.hypothesis: The proposed inversion mechanism may improve usable interruption responses prepared.
experiment.rollback: Remove the temporary practice aid and return to the previous private routine.
